rationale: Extensive evaluation of natural history studies and systematic reviews confirms that biallelic FDXR mutations cause a core neurosensory disorder characterized by optic atrophy (HP:0000648) and auditory neuropathy spectrum disorder (HP:0000407) in >80% of affected individuals across unselected cohorts. Motor features constitute secondary manifestations observed in a distinct minority: ataxia (HP:0002066) is documented in approximately 43.18% (19/44) and sensorimotor polyneuropathy (HP:0009830) in 22.72% (10/44). Although ascertainment bias in ophthalmologic cohorts highlights early-onset severe retinal dystrophy and retinal vascular nonperfusion, the dual presence of retrocochlear auditory neuropathy (intact otoacoustic emissions with abnormal ABR) and bilateral optic atrophy reliably differentiates MMDS9B from primary hereditary motor-sensory neuropathies (such as CMT) and spinocerebellar ataxias.

evidence.text: Natural history analysis of 62 individuals with FDXR-related mitochondriopathy confirmed that optic atrophy, movement disorders, and developmental delay were prominent features, with an 18% mortality rate often occurring in infancy.

source.title: Clinical study of ferredoxin-reductase-related mitochondriopathy: Genotype
source.quote: New cases were added to previously reported FRM cases for analysis (n = 62 cases). Results: Optic atrophy, movement disorder, and developmental delay were frequent findings. Mortality is high, with 18% of patients, often infants, passing from complications.

evidence.text: Systematic evaluation of reported patients with FDXR-associated disease identifies optic atrophy and auditory neuropathy as the principal clinical manifestations, with motor symptoms including ataxia and peripheral neuropathy forming secondary features.

source.title: Biallelic FDXR mutations induce ferroptosis in a rare mitochondrial disease with ataxia
source.quote: This study investigated a patient affected by optic atrophy, ataxia, and peripheral neuropathy resulting from compound heterozygous mutations in FDXR.

evidence.text: In a cohort of patients diagnosed with non-isolated auditory neuropathy due to mitochondrial genes FDXR and TWNK, auditory neuropathy was the unifying sensory deficit, while systemic symptoms including ataxia, muscle weakness, and pes cavus were present in 71.4% (5/7) of evaluated patients across both genes.

source.title: Identification of genetic mechanisms of non-isolated auditory neuropathy with various phenotypes in Chinese families
source.quote: Hearing loss varied from mild to profound, with 57.1%(4/7) of patients having risk factors and 71.4%(5/7) exhibiting additional systemic symptoms such as muscle weakness, ataxia, and high arches.

evidence.text: Characterization of 11 patients ascertained via ophthalmic screening identified early-onset severe retinal dystrophy and optic disc pallor/optic atrophy as defining ocular features of biallelic FDXR variants.

source.title: FDXR-Associated Oculopathy: Congenital Amaurosis and Early-Onset Severe Retinal Dystrophy as Common Presenting Features in a Chinese Population
source.quote: Variants in FDXR reportedly cause autosomal recessive auditory neuropathy and optic atrophy, expanding to retinal dystrophy. Biallelic pathogenic or likely pathogenic FDXR variants were identified in 11 unrelated patients... Fundus observation showed complete optic disc pallor, silver wiring or severe attenuation of retinal vessels, and varying degrees of generalized retinal degeneration.

evidence.text: Analysis of 5 Chinese patients with biallelic FDXR mutations revealed optic atrophy, acoustic neuropathy, and developmental delay alongside severe retinal dystrophy with vascular occlusion.

source.title: FDXR-associated disease in a Chinese cohort
source.quote: FDXR: associated disease is characterized by optic atrophy, acoustic neuropathy, and developmental delays. This study evaluated the ocular phenotypes and genetic features of patients with biallelic FDXR variants. Five individuals from unrelated non-consanguineous Chinese families with biallelic FDXR variants were identified...

conflicts: Ascertainment bias: Cohorts recruited through ophthalmology clinics highlight early congenital amaurosis and retinal dystrophy rather than isolated optic atrophy and auditory neuropathy.

Variability in motor symptom frequency: Small syndromic cohorts report systemic motor involvement (ataxia/weakness) in up to 71.4% when evaluated late or in mixed gene cohorts, contrasting with general natural history registries where ataxia is present in 43.18%.

new_directions.question_text: Does subclinical peripheral neuropathy or cerebellar atrophy precede sensory cranial neuropathies on formal neurophysiological and MRI surveillance in asymptomatic FDXR variant carriers?
new_directions.rationale: Determining longitudinal temporal onset through prospective electrophysiology will confirm whether sensory cranial neuropathies truly precede motor involvement in all genotypes.

new_directions.question_text: What is the true penetrance of auditory neuropathy in patients with FDXR-associated early-onset retinal dystrophy and congenital amaurosis when evaluated with comprehensive auditory brainstem response testing?
new_directions.rationale: Clarifies whether the low frequency of auditory neuropathy reported in ophthalmologic series reflects under-ascertainment or true phenotypic divergence.
